oneLineResult: В прочитанных локусах Афанасия и Григория есть долг, смерть вместо всех, выкуп, очищение мира и победа; нельзя ни свести их к одному предложению возможности спасения, ни автоматически отождествить с поздней полной системой. Прежнее общее «доктрины объёма в текстах нет» отозвано как чрезмерный отрицательный вывод; каждый автор и локус требуют собственного разбора.

cards.notes: Wave 9 PL 75 TEI verification repairs the Bliss English gloss: Mor. I.24.33 (col. 524C, leaf 44) reads sine aestimatione dabatur percipi ('without estimate', not *sine pretio*); III.14.26 (col. 612B, leaf 166) and III.16.29 (col. 614A, leaf 168) juxta carnem pertulit; IV.3.8 (col. 642B, leaf 207) Misertus ergo creator ut redimeret... apostatam angelum repellere. Moralia Part I retains redimeret/redemptionis while rejecting ransom paid to the devil and lacking Anselmian satisfactio.
cards.quoteSafeScope: Only the four Moralia Part I loci collated against PL 75 corrected TEI-XML in Wave 9; not the whole Moralia.

synchronizationReview.positiveFindings: Athanasius joins debt, death instead of all, offering and victory; Gregory30 has ransom. Neither offer-only reduction nor a later confessional identity is automatic.
synchronizationReview.classNormalization: Five axes canonicalized only for ATH-1/NAZ-1, with legacy class labels preserved. Other legacy cards are not silently recertified and remain a schema migration queue; current sourceClasses vocabulary is canonical. No blanket rereading or physical archive availability claim.

commentaryReviewWave4.scope: John 11:52 commentator contexts only; five independent state axes; no full works, printed collation, Greek Chrysostom/Cyril or fresh Prokopenko PDF replay.
findings: Calvin: election before calling; faith/adoption/regeneration distinguished in different respects.
Alford: appointment-to-life expression and John1:12/10:16 among all nations; prophetic-scope difference from Augustine.
Chrysostom: future designation, faithful delivered from coming punishment, one body; English/Latin translations.
Augustine49.27: predestination AND not-yet-children/sheep before faith; Latin and English.
Published Cyril fragment: all mankind, children by creation, gathered through faith into the Church; transmission/attribution qualification retained.
commentaryReviewWave4.method: Recorded after bounded primary-text reading; not an exact time of human reading. Source receipts, locators and read scopes are in the linked control; only their consistency/bytes are mechanically replayable.
commentaryReviewWave4.recheckCommand: python3 -B scripts/atonement_wave4_sources.py (offline); --source-root /external/files for actual new-file byte/extract replay

cyrilJohannineReviewWave5.workingPreference: Gathered believing people of God across nations as referent of John11:52; election/prolepsis can coexist. This is weighed contextual interpretation, not lexical proof, exclusion of all other purposes of death, or erasure of the published Cyril creation reading.
cyrilJohannineReviewWave5.scope: Bounded Cyril English I/VI and attributed VII fragments; eleven Greek Johannine contexts. Four fresh file pins, not replay of old full packages. Details and independent axes belong to source controls.
findings: Creation/incarnation/adoption through faith and Spirit/essential Sonship distinguished.
BookVI objection is distinct from the author reply; common humanity is not identical saving participation.
VII11:52 broad reading preserved; VII11:44 broad release language prevents a whole-author verdict from the BookVI punishment passage.
Greek contextual preference is argued, not proved by lexical counts or a future tense in John17:20.
cyrilJohannineReviewWave5.nextAction: Greek/critical transmission, comparison of VI10:14-15 and VII11:44/52, and bounded OT intertext; no whole-author eschatology/atonement closure.

greekTransmissionReviewWave7.scope: Two bounded Greek digital candidate contexts; 11 verified Git objects plus two byte-matched ZIP members; three rendered web observations. No full-work reading, raw-HTML receipt, print/manuscript collation or new Greek-original quotation.
findings: Liddon reports Greek and Syriac source text and marginal language notices; a particular fragment needs its own language/source identification.
Pearse’s later translated/abridged Pusey account supplies catena leads, not direct manuscript inspection or individual attribution.
Four literal digital differences are retained without silent repair or an assertion of ancient variants/established OCR cause.
The previously read and freshly reread English attributed fragment still supplies the all-human creation and faith-gathering reading.
greekTransmissionReviewWave7.supersedesOnly: Undifferentiated search for a Greek candidate, only for the two located digital contexts and editorial review; no promotion of their evidence class and no closure of O11/C25.
greekTransmissionReviewWave7.nextAction: Acquire and visually collate Randell II133–135 with margins; authenticate candidate Pusey II294–296 and its apparatus; map pg074_0039.1 to printed PG74; trace only the witnesses actually indicated for the target fragment.

greekEditionAndApparatusReviewWave8.scope: 32 byte-verified Git objects across five repositories (8 visually inspected printed page scans of Pusey 1872 Vol. I and 24 OCR/hOCR/XML/JSON witnesses for Pusey Vol. II-III, Migne PG 74, and pipeline provenance) plus five partial web observations. No page-image inspection of Pusey Vol. II pp. 294-296 or PG 74 cols. 69-70, no continuous Greek manuscript for Book VII, and no publication approval.
findings: Pusey 1872 Vol. I printed page scans (title page, Latin Praefatio pp. vii-x, and bound-in Erratum slip) establish the Nicetas and Corderian Greek catena streams, warn of catena compression in Books VII-VIII, and show that Pusey p. ix non-Cyrilline disclaimer on p. 691 a targets the inner allegory on John 11:44 (Vol. II p. 292.15), not 692 a-693 b (John 11:49-52).

Aegean markers 2.294-2.296 match Pusey 1872 Vol. II pp. 294-296; open-greek locus pg074_0039.1 maps to Migne PG 74 cols. 69-70 (1859 leaf 41 = 1863 leaf 039, Aubert 692-693); Randell 1885 Vol. II prints John 11:49-52 on pp. 133-134 without any Syriac notice.

Discrepancies 1, 2, and 4a in OG-JN11 are Qwen3.6 OCR corruptions; Discrepancy 4b is Mai Vatican catena scholium (Reg. Svec. 9 fol. 129) placed in PG 74 col. 69 main column with footnote (2) and relegated to apparatus by Pusey; Discrepancy 3 is a genuine Greek catena split recorded in Pusey II 295 apparatus lines 16-17 (c. l. Cord. Paradise/divine-confession clause vs Nik. Ed. virtue clause), with both recensions preserving death for all humanity, creation sonship, scattering by Satan, and gathering through faith into the Church.

Book VII in Pusey contains 0 Syriac fragments (unlike the four explicitly flagged Syriac scholia at the end of Book VIII on pp. 332-334 = Randell p. 164 From the Syriac), proving John 11:49-52 is transmitted solely through Greek catenae.
greekEditionAndApparatusReviewWave8.supersedesOnly: Wave 7 open edition-mapping, apparatus-identification, and Syriac-medium questions for John 11:49-52; does not supersede visual scan verification of Pusey Vol. II pp. 294-296 or PG 74 cols. 69-70 and does not close O11 or C25.
greekEditionAndApparatusReviewWave8.nextAction: Acquire and visually inspect printed page images (not OCR) of Pusey 1872 Vol. II pp. 294-296 (operacyrilli04cyriuoft frames 306-308) and/or Migne PG 74 cols. 69-70 (patrologiaecurs25hopfgoog leaf 41), and evaluate the theological relationship between Book VII 11:44 and Book VI 10:14-15.

patristicScanAndCyrilComparisonWave9.summary: Wave 9 verifies 21 visual A1 print scans, 3 corrected A1 TEI-XML editions (PL 54, PL 75, First1KGreek Or. 30), and 27 class-C OCR/JSONL witnesses without promoting OCR to VERIFIED_ORIGINAL. Cramer 1841 Vol. II p. 322 (Coislin 23 catena scan, A1) confirms the shorter anonymous scholion on John 11:51-52 displaced after John 12:8; Pusey 1872 Vol. II pp. 294-296 and PG 74 cols. 69-70 remain without page scans, keeping C-25 OPEN. Five-locus comparison of Cyril In Joannem (1:11-13 A1 scan; 8:46-47, 10:14-16, 11:44 C OCR with Praefatio p. ix rejecting the 691A paragraph; 11:49-52) confirms a two-register Johannine grammar (universal creator kinship versus eschatological adoption through faith). GRG-1 is repaired from PL 75 cols. 524C/612B/614A/642B (sine aestimatione dabatur percipi, Misertus ergo creator ut redimeret); LEO-1 (PL 54 + Greek column scans), NAZ-1 (Mason 1899 pp. 140-143 scans; Or. 45.22 remains class C), and CHR-2 (Cramer II p. 320 scan + Hom. 65 OCR) are bound to exact locators.

claimRegister20261026.чтоЭто: реестр доводов лана «fathers»: строка = раздел прозы уровня ## с локатором, классом из её собственных маркеров и отметкой съёма
claimRegister20261026.чтоСчитаетсяДоводом: заголовок «## » в любом .md лана, включая вложенные папки (synthesis/drafts, ot/tools); тело секции — до следующего «## » или до конца файла
claimRegister20261026.приоритет: УДЕРЖИВАЕТСЯ > ОТКРЫТО > ЗАКРЫТО; маркеров нет -> БЕЗ МАРКЕРА; маркер вне классификации -> ошибка съёма, а не «прочее»
claimRegister20261026.метод: scripts/atonement_claim_register.py обходит прозу лана целиком (без выборки), разбирает маркеры вида `ВЕРДИКТ`, сверяет локатор побайтово (файл + номер строки + текст)
claimRegister20261026.правилоСверки: запись лана считается относящейся к файлу, если в ней есть file|path|файл на этот .md;  HOLD-маркеры секций файла обязаны встретиться в маркерах его записей, а маркеры записи обязаны встречаться в прозе лана — так оба учёта проверяют друг друга, а не дополняются до совпадения
